::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Desired resolution of images for a Beamer presentation](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/11203/desired-resolution-of-images-for-a-beamer-presentation), asked by [Little Bobby Tables](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/1527/little-bobby-tables) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-02-16; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I am working on a Beamer presentation for less-technically-inclined audience, so I want to use many visual aids, pictures, stock photos, etc.  Unfortunately, these are mostly raster images, not vector diagrams.
>
> From your experience, what minimal resolution is required so that an image would not appear pixelated when covering a full slide?  I particularly refer to projecting the presentation from a beamer, not viewing it on a computer screen.
:::

I do beamer presentations with lots of art.  While I have not experimented to find minimum values, I get good results from anything 1024x768 pixels and up.  This is flickr's "large" size.  

I mention flickr because it's a good resource for this kind of thing.  Do an advanced search and check the box for Creative Commons-licensed photos.

In case you want to keep looking for vector art, try these: 

 - [Free Vector Resources For Designers in 2011](http://webification.com/free-vector-resources-designers-websites-2011) Showed up in my tweetstream the other day; lists many sites.  I don't know what the licensing is for these.

 - [openclipart.org](http://openclipart.org) has only public-domain works.  You can even search this site within InkScape to make your own modifications.
